a1.text: In 2023, heat killed 2,325 people in the U.S. Texas set a record with 334 deaths, and Harris County had the most.
a1.caption: In 2023, heat killed 2,325 people in the U.S. Texas set a record with 334 deaths, and Harris County had the most.

a2.text: This is HeatWise, built by Aariv Patel, a high-school student from the Houston area.
a2.caption: This is HeatWise, built by Aariv Patel, a high-school student from the Houston area.

a3.text: Weather apps say it feels like 104. But the heat index is a shade number. It leaves out the sun and how hard you're working, and OSHA warns that workers have died of heat stroke at a heat index of only 86.
a3.caption: Weather apps say it feels like 104. But the heat index is a shade number. It leaves out the sun and how hard you're working, and OSHA warns that workers have died of heat stroke at a heat index of only 86.

a4.text: A coach needs to know: is practice safe right now, and if not, when is?
a4.caption: A coach needs to know: is practice safe right now, and if not, when is?

a5.text: Type a city, keep football practice, which uses the Texas U I L heat flags schools must follow, and pick a two-hour practice between 6 AM and 9 PM.
a5.caption: Type a city, keep football practice, which uses the Texas UIL heat flags schools must follow, and pick a two-hour practice between 6 AM and 9 PM.

b1.text: For U.S. places, HeatWise uses the National Weather Service's hourly forecast and estimates W B G T, the heat-stress index U I L, OSHA and the military use.
b1.caption: For U.S. places, HeatWise uses the National Weather Service's hourly forecast and estimates WBGT, the heat-stress index UIL, OSHA and the military use.

b2.text: This is live for Sugar Land today. The card shows this hour's flag and what it means for practice, and the safest window in the next 48 hours.
b2.caption: This is live for Sugar Land today. The card shows this hour's flag and what it means for practice, and the safest window in the next 48 hours.

b3.text: Sunshine data didn't load for this recording, so HeatWise used its simpler estimate and says so on screen.
b3.caption: Sunshine data didn't load for this recording, so HeatWise used its simpler estimate and says so on screen.

b4.text: On the chart, the line is heat stress, the colored bands are the flags, and the green box is the best time.
b4.caption: On the chart, the line is heat stress, the colored bands are the flags, and the green box is the best time.

c1.text: Now a known dangerous day: August 24, 2023, when Houston hit 109 degrees, replayed from the airport's archived reports and labeled as history, not a forecast.
c1.caption: Now a known dangerous day: August 24, 2023, when Houston hit 109 degrees, replayed from the airport's archived reports and labeled as history, not a forecast.

c2.text: The hottest hour hit a black flag: no outdoor workouts. HeatWise moves practice to early morning, while it's still green.
c2.caption: The hottest hour hit a black flag: no outdoor workouts. HeatWise moves practice to early morning, while it's still green.

c3.text: Same weather, different person. Switch to roofing, and HeatWise uses the OSHA and NIOSH limit for heavy work.
c3.caption: Same weather, different person. Switch to roofing, and HeatWise uses the OSHA and NIOSH limit for heavy work.

c4.text: Check acclimatized, and the limit rises from about 73 to 79 degrees. It's personal to the activity, not just the weather.
c4.caption: Check acclimatized, and the limit rises from about 73 to 79 degrees. It's personal to the activity, not just the weather.

d1.text: Below the chart: a water plan from NIOSH, a day-by-day acclimatization schedule, and heat-stroke warning signs with call 9 1 1 up front.
d1.caption: Below the chart: a water plan from NIOSH, a day-by-day acclimatization schedule, and heat-stroke warning signs with call 911 up front.

d2.text: The one-page coach plan puts the whole day on one sheet, here in Spanish for families and crews, ready to print for the clipboard.
d2.caption: The one-page coach plan puts the whole day on one sheet, here in Spanish for families and crews, ready to print for the clipboard.

d3.text: And one click turns the whole app into Spanish.
d3.caption: And one click turns the whole app into Spanish.

e1.text: Is it right? HeatWise was checked against the National Weather Service at eight Houston-area points over 1,472 forecast hours.
e1.caption: Is it right? HeatWise was checked against the National Weather Service at eight Houston-area points over 1,472 forecast hours.

e2.text: Its heat index matched the Weather Service's within 0.28 degrees Fahrenheit.
e2.caption: Its heat index matched the Weather Service's within 0.28 °F.

e3.text: For W B G T, the average bias is about half a degree, on the cautious side, and the typical gap is about 1 degree Fahrenheit. The first version read almost four degrees low, so U.S. places switched to the Weather Service grid.
e3.caption: For WBGT, the average bias is about half a degree, on the cautious side, and the typical gap is about 1 °F. The first version read almost four degrees low, so U.S. places switched to the Weather Service grid.

e4.text: Under the hood: the Lil-yeh-gren physics model for W B G T, and a sliding-window search for the safest window. It's plain JavaScript, free, with no API keys, and 84 passing tests.
e4.caption: Under the hood: the Liljegren physics model for WBGT, and a sliding-window search for the safest window. It's plain JavaScript, free, with no API keys, and 84 passing tests.

e5.text: HeatWise: know the heat, and plan around it. Thanks for watching.
e5.caption: HeatWise: know the heat, and plan around it. Thanks for watching.
